name: Facet
text: Use bold color accents to highlight key metrics in tables and charts. This makes critical numbers pop without clutter, improving visibility and decision speed. The trade-off is slightly reduced visual harmony—some users may find bright colors jarring—but the clarity gain for busy interfaces outweighs this.

name: Pane
text: Bold colors risk accessibility failures for color-blind users and may feel unprofessional in formal reports. A better alternative is using high-contrast grayscale with selective bolding for emphasis—this retains clarity without alienating users. Settle it with a quick A/B test showing task completion time and user preference scores.

name: Facet
text:
Use a single bold accent color (like a saturated blue) for key metrics, paired with a high-contrast grayscale palette for everything else. This keeps the interface clean and professional while ensuring critical numbers stand out without overwhelming the user. The trade-off is slightly reduced visual variety—some users may find the interface less lively—but the clarity and accessibility gains for busy, formal reports outweigh this.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A single bold accent color still fails for color-blind users unless you test it with tools like Coblis—assume nothing. Better: pair the accent with a secondary indicator like bold text or an icon, then measure task completion time and error rates to settle it.
